architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats, recording viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes for each. Accept the combined-axis low-drift hypothesis over H-CORE if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every repeat; 3.80% is half of the 7.61% H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable is measured directly by an isothermal thermal hold and does not depend on a shared thermal-response shape, M-ANCHOR reconstruction, or any rheological regularity transferred from the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family. The selected resin-modified candidate is outside that measured chemistry family, so the 7.61% linear-dilution comparison is a cross-chemistry hypothesis rather than an established regularity. The result supports only a formulation-level rheological claim.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Falsify H-RESIN if SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61% in every repeat, because the result is then not substantially below the H-CORE prediction. Falsify H-CORE if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every repeat, exceeding the declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination resolution. Results with any repeat at or above 3.80% and at least one repeat below 7.61% are intermediate and falsify neither hypothesis under this rule. H-RESIN and H-DUAL cannot be separated by this dual-axis composition.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the matched-window 120 C thermal hold on an acrylic-only candidate with the same 15, 30, 45, and 60 minute sampling and the same per-repeat decision rule, to test whether low drift occurs without the minor tackifier-like axis.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 minutes
judge_normalized.rationale: This experiment directly tests viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C residence, the declared failure mode, without relying on unsupported shared-shape transfer. S1C41 uses the conservative 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor tackifier-like levels, preserves both supported modifier axes for the mitigation test, and provides a checkable comparison between the combined low-drift prediction and the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. Any low-drift result is a combined-axis formulation-level finding, not evidence for a molecular mechanism or a separation of H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate and is in the deterministic top tie, breaking the tie in favor of the smallest sufficient supported dual-axis intervention. I followed the Skeptic's correction that H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled and removed any implication of full three-way separation. The binding audit was respected: modified-chemistry M-ANCHOR cards are inadmissible, whereas this direct M-HOLD-120 card remains admissible.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The candidate lies in the externally supported coarse region for 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, but local hold-drift evidence for resin-modified chemistry is absent.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: The 7.61% H-CORE baseline imports the 9.51% E1 drift through the reactive mass fraction 0.8000; this scaling is a registered testable hypothesis, not a verified resin-family law. No shared thermal-shape extrapolation is used for the primary observable.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The matched-window drift is directly observed with at least two repeats; the declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points. Repeat aggregation and repeat-to-repeat disagreement can affect classification near the thresholds.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 does not control process or preparation state, and the selected plan has moderate process-state risk. Independent repeat preparations provide limited visibility but do not remove state variation.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original PUR reactive-core chemistry represented by E1-E3, with E1 +P treated as a separate verified chemical perturbation. The intended experiment would use a registered resin-modified candidate, so it would not automatically remain inside that audited chemistry support; its hold drift should therefore be measured directly rather than inferred from a shared thermal-shape or one-point state-calibration rule.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with the magnitude of drift potentially depending on modifier chemistry rather than reactive-core dilution alone.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: Original 120 C thermal-hold measurements show SI_15_60 of 9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5 over 15-60 minutes, establishing a large local hold-drift contrast.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local temperature response is sampled at six temperatures from 80 to 130 C for E1-E3, although repeat spread is substantial, and realized viscosity level has repeated E2 measurements showing a 2.80-3.57x max/min spread. By contrast, the isothermal coordinate has only two original formulation-level hold records, E1 and E5, each with four points from 15 to 90 minutes; no candidate hold trajectory or E2 hold is available.
measurement_requirements: Hold the candidate melt at 120 C and measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes, with at least two independent repeats.
Report the raw isothermal trajectories and the matched-window SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 for every repeat.
Record the candidate composition and reactive mass fraction so the observed drift can be compared with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction E1_drift multiplied by phi_r.

Use the predeclared 2 percentage-point discrimination resolution; drift substantially below the linear-dilution prediction, particularly below half that prediction, supports H-RESIN over H-CORE, while agreement within resolution supports H-CORE.
planner.scientific_question: For a matched resin-modified candidate at 120 C, is the 15-60 minute viscosity drift consistent with linear dilution of the reactive core, as predicted by H-CORE, or substantially below that prediction, as required by H-RESIN?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate is resin-modified and outside the chemistry family supporting the local shared thermal-response shape. However, M-HOLD-120 measures the isothermal drift directly and does not infer it from that shape or from an anchor model, so the primary observable remains admissible and scientifically interpretable.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE by demonstrating drift below half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. Because both modifier axes are present, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction. If SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the declared separation threshold.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% does not meet the predeclared H-RESIN acceptance criterion or the stated H-RESIN falsification boundary; it leaves the mechanism unresolved and requires follow-up, including an acrylic-only hold to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely VOI-tied with S1C41, but uses a larger 17.5% acrylic-like modifier burden without increasing hypothesis discrimination, uncertainty reduction, interpretability, or decision relevance.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but the 20% acrylic-like loading is a larger intervention than necessary for the initial direct drift test and provides no additional deterministic information value.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but its 22.5% acrylic-like loading departs further from the characterized reactive core without improving separation of the registered hypotheses.
It is genuinely VOI-tied, but its 25% acrylic-like loading is the largest supported perturbation and is not needed when the same direct hold observable can be obtained at the conservative 15% level.

proposer.reasoning: The declared failure mode is thermal-hold drift, and the least-resolved coordinate is the 120 C isothermal time trajectory. M-HOLD-120 directly observes that coordinate, avoids unsupported shared-shape extrapolation, and has the highest decision relevance and interpretability among the selectable plans. S1C41 tests both independently supported modifier axes in their conservative evidence regions, separates H-CORE from the low-drift alternatives, and minimizes intervention burden within the real deterministic tie.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and directly test the same unresolved isothermal coordinate. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest sufficient modifier burden within the externally supported regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier is the conservative lower-region intervention and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier lies in the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster. It therefore minimizes justified departure from the characterized reactive core while retaining full two-axis coverage.

residual_decision_risk: The resin-modified chemistry is outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared-shape support, although the selected direct hold observable does not depend on that unsupported shape.
The 7.608% H-CORE linear-dilution baseline is a cross-chemistry hypothesis rather than a verified resin-family regularity.
The combined AC1920/TK100 intervention cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and the repeat decision rule is not fully specified.
The deterministic tie among five experiments leaves formulation-level tie-breaking dependent on the scientifically justified minimum-burden rationale rather than on the VOI score itself.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 together, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical predictions at this composition, so the hold cannot distinguish those hypotheses or attribute any suppression to one modifier axis. This does not change which experiment should be run because M-HOLD-120 still directly measures the least-resolved isothermal drift coordinate and can distinguish the combined low-drift result from H-CORE. The result must be interpreted as a combined-axis formulation-level test, with an acrylic-only matched hold required for mechanism attribution. The repeat aggregation rule should also be prespecified.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set. No tested perturbation changes the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, intervention-family and measurement-plan stability are both 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survives the full 0.5-1.5 multiplier sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583. These perturbations are defensible as sensitivity checks, but the resulting stability is stability of the transparent VOI score, not confidence or evidence that the experiment is scientifically correct.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary SI_15_60 quantity remains directly measured and therefore does not depend on the unvalidated shared thermal-response shape or M-ANCHOR. The candidate chemistry itself is outside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family, and the 7.608% H-CORE baseline is an extrapolated hypothesis based on E1 drift scaling rather than a verified resin-family regularity. Direct matched-window holds are sufficient to test that hypothesis, but attribution beyond the observed formulation-level drift requires an acrylic-only comparison and matched process-state control.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can produce SI_15_60 values at 15 and 60 minutes and can therefore reach the stated 7.61% and 3.80% thresholds; the threshold separation is 3.81 percentage points, larger than the declared 2.00% resolution. Attainability is weakened by the unspecified aggregation rule for the two repeats and by the M-HOLD-120 protocol's lack of process-state control, but the criterion is not intrinsically impossible.
leakage_findings: No reliance on the unmeasured validation outcome or formulation identity is evident.
The planned rheological hold cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism stated in H-RESIN; it can only test the registered formulation-level drift prediction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support either resin-wide superlinear suppression or the specific requirement for the minor tackifier axis; it cannot establish which mechanism applies.
objections.objection: The selected S1C41::M-HOLD-120 composition contains both AC1920 at 15% and TK100 at 5%. Its hypothesis_discrimination_detail assigns identical 3.804% predictions to H-RESIN and H-DUAL, a 0 percentage-point difference that is below the declared 2.00% resolution. Thus the experiment cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. The proposer correctly admits this in outcome_interpretation and the falsification_criterion, but contradicts that admission by listing H-DUAL in hypotheses_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result can test the combined intervention against H-CORE, but cannot attribute suppression to either modifier axis or establish the H-DUAL specialization claim.
objections.objection: The formulation_state for S1C41 changes both registered modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0%, leaving a reactive_mass_fraction of 0.8000. Any drift reduction relative to the 7.608% H-CORE prediction is therefore jointly attributable to acrylic-like dilution, TK100, or their interaction. The experiment design implication that this provides 'full two-axis coverage' does not provide causal isolation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may produce a threshold-crossing number without a predeclared rule for handling repeat disagreement, weakening claims that H-CORE or H-RESIN was falsified.
objections.objection: The S1C41 criterion is numerically attainable: 3.80% is below the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction by 3.81 percentage points, exceeding the declared 2.00% resolution, and the protocol records the required 15, 30, 45 and 60 minute values. However, 'stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats' does not specify whether every repeat, the mean, or an uncertainty bound must satisfy the criterion. With M-HOLD-120 marked controls_process_state=false and process_state_risk.score set to 0.75, two uncontrolled preparations could also yield an ambiguous repeat pattern.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A departure from 7.608% could be attributed to resin-specific chemistry, altered process state, or failure of the imported E1 scaling law; the result would not by itself establish the proposed superlinear mechanism.
objections.objection: The primary SI_15_60 observable is directly measured by M-HOLD-120, so it does not reuse the unsupported shared thermal-response shape or M-ANCHOR reconstruction. Nevertheless, the H-CORE comparison imports E1_drift_15_60 of 9.51% from the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family and scales it by phi_r to obtain 7.608% for the resin-modified S1C41 chemistry. The audit explicitly marks the resin-modified family as modified_chemistry_unvalidated and reports no verified shape transfer. Direct drift measurement is admissible, but the cross-chemistry linear-dilution baseline is a tested hypothesis rather than an already supported rheological regularity.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The rheological result could be overstated as proof of a molecular reaction or encounter-frequency pathway that the planned measurement cannot resolve.
objections.objection: No outcome leakage is evident: the payload states that the validation formulation identity and outcome were unavailable, and the selected experiment relies on pre-result E1/E5 data and registered hypotheses. The scope is appropriately rheological rather than molecular. However, the H-RESIN wording about lowering encounter frequency within a non-reactive continuum should remain a formulation-level explanatory hypothesis, because M-HOLD-120 measures only viscosity drift and cannot establish that molecular mechanism.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct M-HOLD-120 protocol for S1C41, but remove H-DUAL from hypotheses_separated and explicitly label the result as a combined-axis test. Add a matched acrylic-only 120 C hold, using the same 15-60 minute window and repeat rule, to test whether low drift occurs without TK100; predefine whether the threshold applies to each repeat or to a specified summary statistic.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 changes AC1920 and TK100 together, while H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical 3.804% predictions at this composition. The primary observable can distinguish the combined low-drift result from H-CORE, but it cannot distinguish the two modifier mechanisms; the contradictory hypotheses_separated field must not be treated as evidence of full three-way discrimination.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived modifier axes, reactive-core anchor, and chemistry/claim boundaries needed to define a matched resin-modified experiment without treating the hypothesis as an optimum.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
